project.name: treetracker-wallet-app
project.description: Treetracker Wallet App is a secure digital token wallet platform built by Greenstand for transparent, verifiable tree-planting and forest-management token transfers, spanning a Next.js web app, an Expo React Native mobile app, and a NestJS backend, unified by Keycloak-based identity and a shared wallet API package.

nodes.name: Wallet Management
nodes.summary: Handles the lifecycle of a user's token wallet: creating a wallet, listing and viewing wallets and their balances, and updating a wallet's profile. It also covers the event-driven automatic provisioning of a wallet when a new user account is created.

businessRules: A wallet has a unique display name, checked for duplicates before creation.
New user accounts are auto-provisioned a wallet via an event-driven queue, not a direct API call from signup.
Wallet profile updates support optional logo and cover image uploads via multipart PATCH.
crossDomainInteractions: Receives an auto-provisioning trigger from Authentication & Identity through the Postgres wallet-creation queue.
Supplies the wallet records that Search & Discovery filters and displays.
Provides the sending and receiving wallets used by Token Transfer.

nodes.name: Create Wallet
nodes.summary: A user creates a new token wallet from the web or native app, with a duplicate-name check and optional redemption of a pending shared action token immediately after creation.

domainMeta.entryPoint: User taps or clicks Create Wallet in the wallet list UI (web or native)

nodes.name: Open Create Wallet Form
nodes.summary: User opens the create-wallet drawer/form from the wallet list.

nodes.name: Check Duplicate Wallet Name
nodes.summary: The wallet page checks the entered name against existing wallets before allowing submission.

nodes.name: Submit Wallet Creation
nodes.summary: The useCreateWallet hook triggers the wallet-creation mutation with the form data.

nodes.name: Create Wallet via API
nodes.summary: The wallet API client posts the wallet name and about text to POST /wallets and returns the created record.

nodes.name: Redeem Pending Shared Token
nodes.summary: If a shared action token was captured from a /claim link, it is redeemed into the newly created wallet.

nodes.name: View and Update Wallet
nodes.summary: A user lists their wallets, opens a wallet to see its balance and details, and can update the wallet's profile (name, about text, visibility, images).

domainMeta.entryPoint: User opens the Wallets list or a specific wallet

nodes.name: Fetch Wallets List
nodes.summary: The useGetWallets hook fetches the user's wallets via GET /wallets.

nodes.name: Render Wallet List
nodes.summary: Each wallet is rendered as a card/row in the wallet list UI.

nodes.name: View Wallet Balance
nodes.summary: The wallet's token balance is displayed in a summary component.

nodes.name: View Wallet Detail Page
nodes.summary: Selecting a wallet opens its detail page showing profile and activity.

nodes.name: Update Wallet Profile
nodes.summary: The wallet's display name, about text, map visibility, and images are updated via a multipart PATCH request.

nodes.name: Automatic Wallet Provisioning
nodes.summary: When a new user account is created in Authentication & Identity, the backend listens for a queue notification and automatically creates a wallet for the new account, decoupling registration from wallet setup.

domainMeta.entryPoint: Postgres NOTIFY on the wallets/creation channel, published after a new Keycloak account is created

nodes.name: Subscribe on Module Init
nodes.summary: The QueueListenerService subscribes to the wallet-creation channel when the NestJS module initializes.

nodes.name: Listen for Wallet-Creation Notifications
nodes.summary: A Postgres LISTEN subscription invokes a callback with the new account id from each parsed message.

nodes.name: Deliver Notification via Postgres NOTIFY
nodes.summary: The shared queue package's subscribe function emits a message event for each NOTIFY payload after acknowledging it.

nodes.name: Fetch Service-Account Token
nodes.summary: The listener obtains a cached Keycloak service-account token to authenticate its call to the wallet API.

nodes.name: Create Wallet via Wallet API
nodes.summary: The listener calls the wallet API with the service-account token to provision a token wallet for the new account.

nodes.name: Token Transfer
nodes.summary: Governs how tree-planting tokens move between wallets: initiating direct or link-shared transfers, responding to incoming transfer notifications, cancelling outgoing transfers, and viewing transfer and token history.

businessRules: A transfer moves either a bundle of generic tokens or a specific set of token ids from one wallet to another.
Pending incoming transfers are surfaced as notifications until the recipient accepts or declines them.
Only the sender can cancel a still-pending outgoing transfer.
Action tokens are signed, time-limited credentials that let a transfer be completed via a shareable link instead of a direct recipient wallet.
crossDomainInteractions: Requires wallets provisioned by Wallet Management as the sending and receiving endpoints of a transfer.
Uses recipient wallets found through Search & Discovery when the sender is choosing who to send to.
Requires an authenticated session token from Authentication & Identity to authorize every transfer API call.

nodes.name: Send Transfer
nodes.summary: A user selects a sending wallet, chooses or searches for a recipient, enters an amount and note, optionally generates a shareable claim link, and submits the transfer.

nodes.name: Choose Sending Wallet
nodes.summary: The user selects which of their wallets to send tokens from.

nodes.name: Search and Select Recipient
nodes.summary: The user searches for and selects the recipient wallet to send to.

nodes.name: Enter Amount and Note
nodes.summary: The user enters the token amount and an optional note before proceeding.

nodes.name: Generate Shareable Action Token
nodes.summary: If sending via a link instead of a direct recipient, a signed, expiring action token is generated.

nodes.name: Submit Transfer
nodes.summary: The useSendTransfer hook triggers the transfer-creation mutation with the chosen wallet, recipient, and amount.

nodes.name: Create Transfer via API
nodes.summary: The wallet API client posts the transfer to POST /transfers as either a token bundle or a list of specific token ids.

nodes.name: Share Token via Link
nodes.summary: A sender shares tokens with someone who may not yet have an account: an action token is generated, embedded in a claim link, and redeemed by the recipient after they register and create their first wallet.

domainMeta.entryPoint: Sender generates a shareable claim link; recipient opens /claim

nodes.name: Sender Generates Action Token
nodes.summary: The sender requests a signed, expiring action token authorizing the transfer, embedded in a shareable link.

nodes.name: Recipient Opens Claim Link
nodes.summary: The recipient visits the public /claim route with the action_token query parameter.

nodes.name: Persist Pending Action Token
nodes.summary: The action token is stored locally so it survives the recipient's signup and login flow.

nodes.name: Recipient Registers or Logs In
nodes.summary: The recipient creates an account or signs in before they can redeem the shared tokens.

nodes.name: Redeem Action Token After Wallet Creation
nodes.summary: Once the recipient has a wallet, the pending action token is redeemed, completing the transfer into their wallet.

nodes.name: View and Respond to Transfer Notifications
nodes.summary: Pending incoming transfers appear as notifications; the recipient opens a notification's detail to accept the transfer and receive the token, or decline it.

nodes.name: List Pending Notifications
nodes.summary: Pending incoming transfer notifications for the user's wallets are listed.

nodes.name: Render Notification Item
nodes.summary: Each notification is rendered with sender initials, title, timestamp, and description.

nodes.name: Open Notification Detail
nodes.summary: Selecting a notification opens its detail view with accept/decline actions.

nodes.name: Accept Transfer
nodes.summary: Accepting calls the transfer-accept API, completing the transfer into the recipient's wallet.

nodes.name: Decline Transfer
nodes.summary: Declining calls the transfer-decline API, returning the tokens to the sender.

nodes.name: View Resulting Token
nodes.summary: After accepting, the user can view the resulting token's details.

nodes.name: Cancel Transfer
nodes.summary: A sender views their outgoing pending transfers and cancels one before the recipient responds.

domainMeta.entryPoint: User opens Transfers list and selects a pending outgoing transfer

nodes.name: View Outgoing Pending Transfers
nodes.summary: The transfers page lists incoming, outgoing, and historical transfers with available actions.

nodes.name: Cancel Transfer via API
nodes.summary: The wallet API client sends DELETE /transfers/:id to cancel a sender-initiated pending transfer.

nodes.name: Remove Transfer from Pending List
nodes.summary: The cancelled transfer is removed from the outgoing pending list in the UI.

nodes.name: View Transfer and Token History
nodes.summary: A user browses their transfer history and drills into a specific transfer or token to see its details and transaction lineage.

domainMeta.entryPoint: User opens Transfers or Token details page

nodes.name: List Transfers
nodes.summary: Transfers are listed via GET /transfers with optional state, wallet, date-range, and sort filters.

nodes.name: View Transfer Detail
nodes.summary: A single transfer's creation/close timestamps and involved tokens are shown.

nodes.name: List Tokens in Transfer
nodes.summary: The specific tokens included in a transfer are fetched via GET /transfers/:id/tokens.

nodes.name: View Token Detail
nodes.summary: A single token's details are shown alongside its transaction history.

nodes.name: View Token Transaction Lineage
nodes.summary: A token's full transaction (lineage) history is fetched via GET /tokens/:id/transactions.

nodes.name: Search & Discovery
nodes.summary: Lets users find wallets, most often to choose a recipient for a token transfer, by typing a query or displaying a scannable QR code that others can search for.

businessRules: Search results are sectioned into matching, non-matching, or category-grouped results with computed relevance sorting.
A wallet's QR code is a shareable identifier that lets other users find and select it via search.
crossDomainInteractions: Searches and filters wallet records owned by Wallet Management.
Feeds the recipient-selection step of Token Transfer's send flow.

nodes.name: Search Wallets
nodes.summary: A user types a query in the search box; the app derives sectioned, category-grouped results and lets the user open a wallet's details.

domainMeta.entryPoint: User types in the header/search screen search box

nodes.name: Enter Search Query
nodes.summary: The user types a query into the header or dedicated search screen.

nodes.name: Update Search State
nodes.summary: Query text, loading flags, recent searches, and category selection are tracked in shared search atoms.

nodes.name: Derive Sectioned Results
nodes.summary: A hook derives UI-ready matching, non-matching, or category-grouped results plus display metadata.

nodes.name: Render Search Results
nodes.summary: Results are rendered as a list of selectable items.

nodes.name: Select Result and Open Wallet Detail
nodes.summary: Selecting a result opens the corresponding wallet's detail modal or page.

nodes.name: Display Wallet QR Code
nodes.summary: A user displays their own wallet's QR code so another user can scan or search for it as a transfer recipient.

domainMeta.entryPoint: User opens their wallet's QR code display

nodes.name: Render Wallet QR Code
nodes.summary: The user's wallet identifier is rendered as a scannable QR code.

nodes.name: Display on Native Search Tab
nodes.summary: The native app's search tab shows the same QR display alongside search results.

nodes.name: Peer Searches for the Wallet
nodes.summary: Another user finds the wallet through the search flow, e.g. after scanning the code.

nodes.name: Authentication & Identity
nodes.summary: Manages user registration, login, session token lifecycle, and logout, all delegated to a centralized Keycloak identity provider, plus the backend's own service-account credentials for calling Keycloak's admin API.

businessRules: User registration and login are delegated to a hosted Keycloak instance rather than handled with local credential storage.
The backend caches a single service-account token, refreshing it only when missing or expired, to call Keycloak's admin API.
Session tokens are persisted through a cross-platform storage adapter: session storage on web, AsyncStorage on native.
crossDomainInteractions: Issues the session tokens that Token Transfer and Wallet Management require to authorize API calls.
New account creation publishes the queue event that Wallet Management consumes to auto-provision a wallet.

nodes.name: User Registration
nodes.summary: A new user registers via Keycloak's hosted registration page or an in-app form; the backend creates the account in Keycloak and a wallet-creation event is published for downstream provisioning.

domainMeta.entryPoint: POST /api/auth/signup (web) or Keycloak hosted registration redirect

nodes.name: Redirect to Registration
nodes.summary: The signup route redirects the browser to Keycloak's hosted registration page.

nodes.name: Validate and Submit Registration Form
nodes.summary: Registration form input is trimmed and validated before being posted to the treetracker user API.

nodes.name: Create Account in Keycloak
nodes.summary: The backend user service creates the account via Keycloak's admin REST API using a service-account token.

nodes.name: Publish Wallet-Creation Notification
nodes.summary: A notification is published on the wallet-creation channel so a wallet can be provisioned asynchronously.

nodes.name: Show Account-Created Confirmation
nodes.summary: The user is shown a confirmation page after their account and wallet are set up.

nodes.name: User Login
nodes.summary: A user logs in via Keycloak's hosted login page or an in-app form, and the app handles the resulting OIDC callback.

domainMeta.entryPoint: POST /api/auth/login (web) or Keycloak hosted login redirect

nodes.name: Redirect to Keycloak Hosted Login
nodes.summary: The login route redirects the browser to Keycloak's hosted login page.

nodes.name: Validate and Submit Credentials
nodes.summary: Login form input is trimmed and validated before being posted to the treetracker user API.

nodes.name: Password-Grant Login Against Keycloak
nodes.summary: The backend user service performs a password-grant login against Keycloak's OpenID Connect endpoint.

nodes.name: Handle OIDC Callback
nodes.summary: The callback route waits for the auth context to be ready then routes to home or login based on authentication state.

nodes.name: Session Token Management
nodes.summary: The app initializes the Keycloak client on mount, mirrors and persists the resulting token, keeps it refreshed, and clears it on logout.

nodes.name: Initialize Keycloak Client
nodes.summary: Keycloak is initialized on mount and its ready/authenticated state exposed via a context provider.

nodes.name: Persist Token
nodes.summary: The auth token is persisted in a cross-platform storage adapter shared by web and native.

nodes.name: Auto-Refresh Token
nodes.summary: The provider sets up automatic token refresh so the session stays valid.

nodes.name: Log Out and Clear Token
nodes.summary: Logging out clears the persisted authentication token and redirects to Keycloak logout.

nodes.name: Backend Service-to-Service Auth
nodes.summary: The backend obtains and caches its own Keycloak service-account token via the client-credentials flow so it can call Keycloak's admin API on behalf of users.

domainMeta.entryPoint: Backend service needs a Keycloak service-account token to call an admin API

nodes.name: Request Service-Account Token
nodes.summary: The auth service requests a service-account token from Keycloak's token endpoint using client credentials.

nodes.name: Cache and Reuse Token
nodes.summary: The token is cached and only refreshed when missing or expired, avoiding a token request on every call.

nodes.name: Call Keycloak Admin API
nodes.summary: The cached token authorizes calls to Keycloak's admin REST API, e.g. to create a user account.

edges.description: New Keycloak account creation publishes a queue notification that Wallet Management consumes to auto-provision a wallet.
Session tokens issued during login authorize every wallet and transfer API call.
A wallet must exist before it can send, receive, or hold pending transfers.
Search results supply the recipient wallet chosen when sending a transfer.
Search filters and displays the same wallet records that Wallet Management fetches and manages.
